query: We run n8n in queue mode (1 main + 3 workers, Docker Compose, Caddy) on root@203.0.113.10. I want to turn on the new Agents feature. What do I need to change?
expected_behavior: Activate n8n-self-hosting and read QUEUE_MODE.md before answering — modules + env parity live there
Identify N8N_ENABLED_MODULES=agents as the flag (a comma-separated opt-in list; agents is NOT on by default)
Insist the flag reaches the WORKERS as well as the main — in the template that means the shared x-n8n-env anchor, not the main service's own environment block

Explain WHY: the main serves the UI/REST so the feature looks configured there, but workers execute the workflows; with OFFLOAD_MANUAL_EXECUTIONS_TO_WORKERS=true even a manual test run goes to a worker
Name the characteristic symptom of getting it wrong: a TypeORM EntityMetadataNotFoundError (e.g. No metadata for "Agent" was found) at runtime, not at boot
Apply the change with docker compose up -d (recreating main AND workers), not via a wrapper script that runs docker compose pull — that would bundle an unplanned n8n upgrade into a settings change
Verify with an env-parity diff between main and worker containers, expecting only the public-URL/proxy vars to differ

Be honest that the docs mark queue mode as unsupported for agents, that this is unsupported territory which an upgrade can break, and that agent knowledge base additionally needs the sandbox/Daytona vars on workers
notes: Regression guard for a real production failure: the module flag was added to the main service only, the agent picker still populated from the main, and every execution of the Message an Agent node died on a worker with EntityMetadataNotFoundError. The skill must teach env parity as a rule, not just this one flag.
